fixes.explanation: Right there in the verse: “In darkness they do their works…” The whole plan is to hide where nobody can look. It's like sneaking a cookie off the cooling rack with the lights off, then standing there with crumbs on your shirt like it's a secret. Isaiah opens that line with “Woe.”
I see why you'd guess it, friend, but Isaiah never puts them in the temple courts. He says “In darkness they do their works…” These folks are digging deep to hide their plans from the LORD.

Clay! Isaiah says it's turned upside down “…as if the potter were regarded as clay.” The one doing the shaping gets treated like the lump on the wheel. That's like a cookie turning to me and saying, "I stamped you." It's backwards, and Isaiah says so.

Not quite, friend. Isaiah asks, “In a very short time, will not Lebanon become an orchard…” That's a very short time, not a long one. It's like sliding dough into the oven and having the batch done before you finish wiping the counter.

Close is sneaky, friend, but it doesn't fit. Isaiah says “…out of the deep darkness the eyes of the blind will see.” Eyes that close would be the opposite of what's promised. The promise is that the eyes of the blind will see.
That's it. Isaiah says, “The humble will increase their joy in the LORD, and the poor among men will rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.” Notice the word increase. Their joy goes up.
Evil is right. Isaiah says “…all who look for evil will be cut down…” These are people who go searching for it. I think this one is heavy, baker.
Peace is a good thing to look for, so I get the guess. But Isaiah says “…all who look for evil will be cut down…” The word that goes in this blank is evil.
Right. Isaiah says they are the ones “…who with false charges deprive the innocent of justice.” A charge that isn't true, used to take what an innocent person is owed. I think this one hurts, baker.

Hold on, friend, it goes the other way. The LORD who redeemed Abraham says, “No longer will Jacob be ashamed and no more will his face grow pale.” That's a promise that the shame stops. His face will no longer grow pale.
That's the one. When Jacob sees his children around him, the LORD calls them “…the work of My hands…” Hands are what a maker uses.

Honor! The LORD says, “…they will honor My name, they will sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and they will stand in awe of the God of Israel.” That's three things in a row. That's what He says about Jacob's children once Jacob sees them around him.

Question is a fair guess, baker, but the LORD says “…they will honor My name…” Question isn't the word in this blank. The same verse says they will sanctify the Holy One of Jacob and stand in awe of the God of Israel.
True! The last line says, “…those who grumble will accept instruction.” The grumblers come around. In the same line, the wayward in spirit come to understanding.
